text: dsh-session-journal 是面向 DSH 网页端的会话工作日志插件，在右侧边栏展示会话当前进展、工作项、阶段、结果、待办和决定，并提供会话标题旁的阶段提示。插件读取会话事件，按轮收集消息、工具调用和文件等事实，可通过当前会话的模型生成摘要并归纳工作项；没有摘要模型时仍可按规则显示阶段。日志条目可跳回对应对话轮次，摘要缓存在 DSH 本地目录。

dsh-session-journal is a DSH web plugin for reviewing session progress in the right sidebar. It groups turns into work items, shows phases, results, decisions and open items, and links entries back to turns. The session model can summarize turns; rule-based phases work without it.
想在 DSH 右侧边栏查看每个会话做过的工作和当前进展。
I want a session summary that links each work item back to its conversation turns.
dsh-session-journal 的功能「会话工作日志」：在网页端右侧栏按工作项展示会话进展、阶段、结果、未解决事项和决定，并显示当前状态。打开日志标签页即可查看。
dsh-session-journal 的功能「按轮摘要与跳转」：插件读取会话事件并整理每轮事实，可调用会话模型生成阶段摘要，再把日志中的轮次链接回对话位置。用户在日志中点击轮次即可跳转。
dsh-session-journal 使用前须知：模型摘要会将会话整理内容发送给 DSH 模型提供方；设置 SESSION_JOURNAL_MODEL=off 可仅按规则整理（见 lib/index.js:82-99）。
dsh-session-journal 的维护与更新元数据：活跃维护；距最后推送 6 天；提交数 10；更新频次 unknown；近 90 天提交 未知；开放 Issue 未知；仓库健康分 62/100（置信度 low）。

dsh-session-journal README · dsh-session-journal：A [DeepSeek Harness (DSH)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) Web plugin that keeps a **work journal** for each session in the right sidebar. Long sessions scroll away: requirements were discussed, code was written, reviewed three times, fixed and tested, and by then the start is far out of view. The journal shows what the session has worked on, where each piece of work stands, and lets you jump back to any turn in the chat.

[中文文档](README.zh.md)

dsh-session-journal README · What you get：- **Now**: whether the session is running, the current phase (for example `Review #2`), a one-line status, and a highlighted "Your turn" box when the agent stopped to wait for you. Totals for the session: open items, decisions, turns, time, changed files and lines, tests passed.
- **Work items**: the session's turns grouped by purpose (one card per thing it worked on), not by time. Each card shows its status, the turns it covers, files and tests, and counts of what is still **open** and what was **decided**, so a card marked done with loose ends says so. Expanded, it shows the goal, the result, the open items, the decisions, and two lists:
  - **Jump to a turn**: one row per turn with what you asked and the phases it went through. Click a row to scroll the chat to the start of that turn (earlier history is loaded first when needed).
  - **Changed files**: file name, directory, lines added and removed, the phases that touched it. Click to open the file in the sidebar preview.
- **Header chip**: the current work item and phase next to the session title; click it to open the journal.
- English and Chinese UI, following the DSH language setting

dsh-session-journal README · Usage：Open a session and pick **Work log** on the right sidebar's start page, or click the chip next to the session title. Expand a work item to see its open items and decisions; open **Jump to a turn** and click a row to scroll the chat to that turn. Change the summary language in the panel footer.

dsh-session-journal README · How it works：1. **Facts** (`lib/collector.js`): the plugin reads the session's append-only event log through DSH's `sessionQuery` service, so compacted history is still there. Per turn it extracts the user's message, every tool call, file edits with line counts, test commands and their exit codes, review delegations, questions to the user, and the todo list.
2. **Per-turn summaries** (`lib/summarizer.js`): each finished turn is summarized once by a model into phases (from a fixed list: requirements, research, design, build, review, fix, test, debug, ship, discussion), a short title and result per phase, the decisions made, and what was left open. Text the user pasted from elsewhere (another session's panel, logs, someone else's message) is treated as material, not as a request.
3. **Work items** (`lib/outline.js`): once every finished turn has a summary, one more call groups the turns into 1 to 6 work items and writes each item's status, result, open items and decisions. It sees the whole session, so problems solved in later turns do not linger as open. It is redone when the summaries change, which is about one call per new turn.
4. **When it updates**
dsh-session-journal README · How it works：Without a model the journal still works: phases come from rules (edits, tests, reviews) and the whole session is one work item.

dsh-session-journal README · Model and cost：By default each session is summarized with **that session's own provider and model**. Summary calls are separate requests with their own small context; they never touch the conversation or its cache. Costs, roughly: one call per finished turn (a few thousand input tokens), and one outline call per new turn (5k to 20k input tokens on long sessions). In the background, only sessions that are being worked on cost anything; idle sessions are not touched (opening the panel on one still summarizes any turns it lacks). The first turn to end after installing or upgrading the plugin also summarizes that session's earlier turns that have no summary yet, and so does the first turn of a forked session, for the turns it inherited.

dsh-session-journal README · Model and cost：To use one fixed, usually cheaper, model for every session, set both `SESSION_JOURNAL_PROVIDER` and `SESSION_JOURNAL_MODEL` in DSH's launch environment (for example `$DSH_HOME/.env`); setting only one of them has no effect:

```bash
SESSION_JOURNAL_PROVIDER=<provider id>
SESSION_JOURNAL_MODEL=<model id>
SESSION_JOURNAL_EFFORT=low        # reasoning effort; "default" leaves it to the route

dsh-session-journal README · SESSION_JOURNAL_MODEL=off       # no model calls, rules only：```

Restart DSH after changing them.
section: SESSION_JOURNAL_MODEL=off       # no model calls, rules only

text: dsh-session-journal README · Jumping to a turn：DSH has no public "scroll to turn" API for plugins. The chat view has its own turn rail, a row of ticks at the right edge of the transcript, one per turn. The journal finds the tick for the turn and clicks it, so the chat does the scrolling and any history loading itself.

dsh-session-journal README · Jumping to a turn：- This relies on the chat view's markup, not on a contract. If a DSH update changes the rail, clicking a turn shows a note instead of jumping; nothing else breaks.
- The rail hides itself when the chat column is narrower than 900px, which is normal with the right sidebar open. The journal renders it invisibly for the moment of the click and then hands it back.
- The main area must show the Chat view. On other views the journal asks you to switch back first.
dsh-session-journal README · Requirements：DSH `>=0.2.2-alpha.2 <0.3.0-0` (0.2.x, including its prereleases), Node `>=22.19`.

dsh-session-journal README · Install：```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add github:Edison-A-N/dsh-session-journal
```

The package ships its own bundle patch (`dsh.bundle.patch` + `cordis.patch.yml`), so the CLI and the Web UI's Plugins page load it in one step. Restart DSH, reload the page, open a session, and pick **Work log** on the right sidebar's start page (or click the chip in the session header).

dsh-session-journal README · Known limitations：- Grouping into work items is done by a model and is not always how you would split the work; for example a release step may come out as its own item.
- While a turn is running, a work item's open items can lag one turn behind; they catch up when the turn ends and is summarized.
- Files outside the session's workspace are listed but cannot be previewed in the sidebar.
- The first time you open a long session that has no cache yet, summarizing every turn takes a minute or two. Until then the panel shows rule-based phases.

dsh-session-journal README · Development：```bash
pnpm install
pnpm run build   # bundles client/src into lib/client.js
pnpm test
```

`lib/client.js` is committed, because DSH loads it as-is; rebuild it in the same commit as any change under `client/src`.

Bug reports and pull requests are welcome on [GitHub](https://github.com/Edison-A-N/dsh-session-journal/issues). Please include the DSH version, the browser, and what the panel showed.
